newsitem.title: UK: UK Govt says cannot give parl't Easter break dates.
newsitem.headline: UK Govt says cannot give parl't Easter break dates.

text.p: The government is unable to detail the dates of parliament's Easter recess yet, leader of the house Tony Newton told the House of Commons on Thursday.
The announcement is likely to increase speculation about when Prime Minister John Major will announce the election date.
Newton, giving details of parliamentary business until Monday, March 24, said: "I am not yet in a position to make a definitive statement about recess dates."
The latest the election can legally be held is May 22 but Major has said he would not call it later than May 1. That is thought to be his preferred date and is only seven weeks away.
But if Major calls a May 1 poll, he must dissolve parliament at least 17 working days beforehand -- April 8 or earlier.

Journalists had been expecting details of the Easter break, hoping it would give them a clue as to when Major -- trailing Labour by around 20 points in polls -- would call the election. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
